units.title: Describing Data
units.blurb: Display one-variable data and summarize its center, spread and shape.

units.title: The Normal Distribution
units.blurb: Use the normal model to find proportions and percentiles.

units.title: Two-Variable Data
units.blurb: Describe association, fit least-squares lines, and judge a model with residuals.

units.title: Collecting Data
units.blurb: Choose samples, avoid bias, and design experiments.

units.title: Probability Rules
units.blurb: Use the addition and multiplication rules, conditional probability and counting.

units.title: Random Variables
units.blurb: Describe random outcomes with distributions, means and standard deviations.

units.title: Sampling Distributions
units.blurb: See how statistics vary from sample to sample.

units.title: Inference
units.blurb: Estimate with confidence intervals and test claims with significance tests.

topics.title: Categorical and Quantitative Variables
topics.short: Tell whether data are labels or measured numbers.
topics.trouble: Students treat number labels, like zip codes, as quantitative.

topics.title: Displaying Categorical Data
topics.short: Read bar graphs, pie charts and relative frequencies.

topics.title: Histograms and Shape
topics.short: Describe shape as symmetric, skewed, unimodal or bimodal.
topics.trouble: Students call a distribution skewed toward the side where most of the data sit, when skew is named for the long tail.

topics.title: Mean, Median and Resistance
topics.short: The median resists outliers; the mean does not.
topics.trouble: Students expect the mean and median to match even in skewed data.

topics.title: Standard Deviation
topics.short: A typical distance from the mean.
topics.trouble: Students confuse standard deviation with range, or forget to take the square root of the variance.

topics.title: Five-Number Summary and Outliers
topics.short: Use the 1.5 × IQR rule to flag outliers.

topics.title: Comparing Distributions
topics.short: Compare shape, center and spread in context.
topics.trouble: Students compare centers but say nothing about spread or overlap.

topics.title: z-Scores and Percentiles
topics.short: z tells how many standard deviations a value is from the mean.
topics.trouble: Students subtract in the wrong order and get the sign of z backward.

topics.title: Shifting and Scaling Data
topics.short: Adding a constant moves the center; multiplying scales center and spread.
topics.trouble: Students think adding 5 to every value increases the standard deviation.

topics.title: The Normal Curve and the 68-95-99.7 Rule
topics.short: About 68%, 95% and 99.7% of values lie within 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations.
topics.trouble: Students apply the rule to strongly skewed data.

topics.title: Areas under the Normal Curve
topics.short: Find the proportion below, above or between values.
topics.trouble: Students report the area to the left when the question asks for the area to the right.

topics.title: Finding Values from Percentiles
topics.short: Work backward from an area to a z-score to a value.

topics.title: Describing Scatterplots
topics.short: Describe direction, form, strength and unusual points.

topics.title: The Correlation Coefficient
topics.short: r measures the direction and strength of a linear pattern.
topics.trouble: Students read r as the slope, or call a strong curved pattern "no relationship" because r is near 0.

topics.title: The Least-Squares Regression Line
topics.short: The line that makes the sum of squared residuals smallest.
topics.trouble: Students predict far outside the range of the data.

topics.title: Interpreting Slope and Intercept
topics.short: Say what the slope and intercept mean in context, with units.
topics.trouble: Students state a predicted change as an exact change for every individual.

topics.title: Residuals and Residual Plots
topics.short: A good linear fit leaves residuals with no pattern.
topics.trouble: Students take a high r as proof the linear model is right, ignoring a curved residual plot.

topics.title: r² and the Quality of Fit
topics.short: r² is the fraction of the variation in y explained by the line.
topics.trouble: Students read r² = 0.64 as "64% of the points are on the line."

topics.title: Outliers and Influential Points
topics.short: Some points pull the line toward themselves.

topics.title: Fitting Exponential and Power Models
topics.short: Use logs to straighten curved data.

topics.title: Correlation, Causation and Lurking Variables
topics.short: Association alone does not show cause and effect.
topics.trouble: Students conclude that ice cream sales cause drownings because the two are correlated.

topics.title: Sampling Methods
topics.short: Simple random, stratified, cluster and systematic samples.

topics.title: Bias in Sampling and Surveys
topics.short: Spot undercoverage, nonresponse and leading questions.
topics.trouble: Students think a larger sample fixes a biased sampling method.

topics.title: Observational Studies and Experiments
topics.short: Only a randomized experiment can show cause and effect.
topics.trouble: Students draw causal conclusions from an observational study.

topics.title: Designing Experiments
topics.short: Use control, random assignment, replication and blocking.
topics.trouble: Students confuse random sampling, which supports generalizing, with random assignment, which supports cause and effect.

topics.title: Evaluating Statistical Reports
topics.short: Judge claims in the news by how the data were produced.

topics.title: Events, Unions, Intersections and Complements
topics.short: Describe events with "or," "and" and "not."
topics.trouble: Students treat "A or B" as "exactly one of A and B."

topics.title: The Addition Rule
topics.short: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B).
topics.trouble: Students add the probabilities without subtracting the overlap.

topics.title: Conditional Probability
topics.short: P(A ∣ B) is the probability of A among the outcomes where B happened.
topics.trouble: Students confuse P(A ∣ B) with P(B ∣ A).

topics.title: Conditional Probability from Two-Way Tables
topics.short: Divide by the row or column total that matches the condition.
topics.trouble: Students divide by the grand total instead of the total for the given condition.

topics.title: Independent Events
topics.short: A and B are independent when P(A ∣ B) = P(A).
topics.trouble: Students think mutually exclusive events are independent, when knowing one happened rules out the other.

topics.title: The General Multiplication Rule
topics.short: P(A and B) = P(A) · P(B ∣ A).
topics.trouble: Students multiply unconditional probabilities when drawing without replacement.

topics.title: Bayes' Rule
topics.short: Reverse a conditional probability with a tree or a table.
topics.trouble: Students ignore how rare a condition is and trust a positive test result too much.

topics.title: Permutations
topics.short: Count arrangements when order matters.
topics.trouble: Students use a permutation when order does not matter, counting each group several times.

topics.title: Combinations
topics.short: Count selections when order does not matter.

topics.title: Probability with Counting
topics.short: Use permutations and combinations to find probabilities.

topics.title: Discrete Random Variables
topics.short: List values and their probabilities in a table.
topics.trouble: Students build a probability table whose probabilities do not add to 1.

topics.title: Expected Value
topics.short: The long-run average outcome: Σ x · P(x).
topics.trouble: Students think the expected value must be a value the variable can take.

topics.title: Standard Deviation of a Random Variable
topics.short: Measure how much a random variable typically varies from its mean.

topics.title: Sums and Differences of Random Variables
topics.short: Means add; for independent variables, variances add.
topics.trouble: Students add standard deviations, or subtract variances for a difference.

topics.title: The Binomial Distribution
topics.short: Count successes in n independent trials with the same p.
topics.trouble: Students use the binomial model when trials are not independent or n is not fixed.

topics.title: The Geometric Distribution
topics.short: Count the trials until the first success.

topics.title: Continuous Random Variables
topics.short: Probability is area under a density curve.
topics.trouble: Students think P(X = 3) is positive for a continuous variable.

topics.title: Decisions with Expected Value
topics.short: Compare games, insurance and strategies by expected payoff.

topics.title: Is the Model Consistent? Simulation
topics.short: Use simulation to judge whether data fit a model.

topics.title: Sampling Distribution of a Proportion
topics.short: Sample proportions center on p with spread √(p(1 − p)/n).
topics.trouble: Students confuse the distribution of one sample's data with the distribution of the statistic.

topics.title: Sampling Distribution of a Mean and the CLT
topics.short: Sample means are close to normal for large n, with spread σ/√n.
topics.trouble: Students think the central limit theorem makes the data themselves normal.

topics.title: Confidence Intervals for a Proportion
topics.short: Estimate ± margin of error.
topics.trouble: Students say there is a 95% chance the true value is in this particular interval.

topics.title: Margin of Error and Sample Size
topics.short: Quadrupling the sample size halves the margin of error.
topics.trouble: Students think doubling the sample size halves the margin of error.

topics.title: Confidence Intervals for a Mean
topics.short: Use t when the population standard deviation is unknown.

topics.title: The Logic of Significance Tests
topics.short: Ask how surprising the data would be if the null hypothesis were true.
topics.trouble: Students read the p-value as the probability that the null hypothesis is true.

topics.title: Testing a Claim about a Proportion
topics.short: Carry out a one-proportion z test.
topics.trouble: Students write hypotheses about the sample statistic instead of the population parameter.

topics.title: Testing a Claim about a Mean
topics.short: Carry out a one-sample t test.

topics.title: Type I and Type II Errors and Power
topics.short: Weigh the two kinds of mistakes a test can make.
topics.trouble: Students mix up which error is rejecting a true null hypothesis.

topics.title: Comparing Two Treatments by Randomization
topics.short: Reshuffle groups to see whether a difference could be chance.

topics.title: Two-Sample Intervals and Tests
topics.short: Compare two proportions or two means.
topics.trouble: Students treat paired data as two independent samples.

topics.title: Chi-Square Tests
topics.short: Test goodness of fit and association in two-way tables.
topics.trouble: Students use percentages instead of counts in the chi-square statistic.

topics.title: Inference for the Slope of a Regression Line
topics.short: Test and estimate the true slope from sample data.
